findings.finding: Intapp guided Q1 FY27 above the street (EPS $0.39-0.41 vs ~$0.28-0.34 consensus at the time; revenue $159.3-160.3m vs ~$157.4m) and beat its last quarter (Q4 non-GAAP EPS $0.41 vs $0.36 consensus, cloud ARR +29% to $495.7m, NRR 123%, $1m+ ARR clients 142 vs 109); a beat of the guided range is the likely print, but it lands inside what the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 4 2026 beat on EPS and cloud metrics: +12.75%; May 2026 -4.19%; Feb 2026 -13.2%; Aug 2025 +15.52%; May 2025 -6.59%; Feb 2025 -1.21% (baseline). Only 2 of 6 up; the two up moves were August prints that carried a new fiscal-year guide, the Feb/May prints sold off.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the guide is public and has been for 12 weeks and the stock rose 30% in 20 sessions. What would remain unpriced is the size of the beat on cloud ARR, for which no consensus is published; if the market had priced a large ARR beat the stock would already sit above its 52-week high (it is 4% below).
findings.independence: Chartmill on the Q4 beat and cloud metrics (https://www.chartmill.com/news/INTA/Chartmill-52645-Intapp-NASDAQINTA-Rises-After-Q4-EPS-Beat-and-Strong-Cloud-Metrics); same underlying company release, so not independent evidence about Q1.

findings.finding: The stock enters the print up 30.6% in 20 sessions and 4.2% from its 52-week high, a move that coincides with a sector-wide software rerating (S&P software & services index at its 2026 high on 2026-10-06 as AI-disruption fears faded) and with no company-specific fundamental release in the window, so the bar for the quarter has been raised by price rather than by information; Kalkine (2026-10-20) reports the average analyst price objective is below the share price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print fell 13.2% and May 2026 fell 4.19% during the 'SaaSpocalypse' period; the Aug 2026 print rose 12.75% from a low base (shares ~$33 pre-print). No case in the 6-print history of a print coming off a +30% 20-day run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself, so the run-up is fully visible; what is not settled is whether a guide-level beat justifies a stock that has already re-rated with its sector. If the market were braced for a sell-the-news reaction the 25-delta skew would carry a put premium; it reads -0.09 (balanced), so the option market is not leaning either way.
findings.independence: Kalkine Media 2026-10-20 (https://kalkinemedia.com/us/stocks/technology/intapp-nasdaqinta-soars-toward-highs-can-the-climb-continue): shares near yearly high, average price objective below price. Baseline tape (run_up_20d 30.6, pct_from_52w_high -4.21). Short interest in 2026 not found; 2025 level ~3% of float, not crowded, so no squeeze offset is evident.

findings.finding: During the reported quarter (Jul-Sep) and after, Intapp put Celeste into general availability (2026-07-15), announced an OpenAI collaboration/ChatGPT Enterprise plug-in (2026-09-17) and logged DealCloud+Celeste wins at Forvis Mazars Capital Advisors (2026-09-22) and Carr, Riggs & Ingram M&A Advisors (2026-10-20); AI products were already >20% of Q4 net new bookings. The announced in-quarter wins are mid-market advisory/accounting firms, with no Am Law 100 win announced in the quarter (Ropes & Gray was May, Q4).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OpenAI plug-in news moved the stock +2.5% pre-open on 2026-09-18 (Investing.com); the March 2026 Anthropic/Harvey deals were credited with a ~12% gain (TIKR). AI-attach commentary was part of the Aug +12.75% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Each announcement is public and partly priced (the OpenAI news moved the stock on the day). What is not visible is how much of Q1 net new cloud ARR the GA of Celeste contributed; if the market had a number it would be a published AI ARR or bookings consensus, and none exists.
findings.independence: Investing.com 2026-09-18 on the OpenAI plug-in reaction (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-intapp-stock-climbing-today-93CH-4907409). Company-sourced announcements; proxy for bookings, not a bookings number.

findings.finding: EDGAR shows a steady run of insider Form 144/Form 4 sales through the quarter and into the print (Form 144 2026-10-20, Form 4s 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22, after the CEO sold 65,802 shares at ~$41.20 under a 10b5-1 plan in August); routine plan selling, not a cluster with information content.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hall's recurring 10b5-1 sales have accompanied both up and down prints; no measurable association.
findings.why_not_priced: Public filings; aggregators report them. Likely fully priced and near zero information, filed for completeness.
